In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
angler surveys and FIS performed equally well at capturing the size composition of the three species sampled in both RFH’s.

the angler survey and fishery-independent survey methods are equally effective at capturing the length spectrum of the species examined, and therefore, the two methods are complementary and can be used in a combined manner for length-based stock assessment and monitoring in partially protected marine areas.

the angler surveys and the fishery-independent surveys were comparable for the species and locations considered, but that angler surveys captured a more representative size spectrum for Acanthorpagrus spp. and Dusky Flatheads, and that fishery-independent surveys captured a more accurate representation of the size spectrum for Sand Whiting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
angler surveys and FIS are complementary and should be used in combination to provide the most accurate and complete picture of the length composition of a species.

angler surveys and fisheries-independent surveys both have their place in the assessment of partially protected fish populations, and the use of both methods is likely to provide the most comprehensive picture of the population.

the angler survey and fishery-independent survey approaches are complimentary in terms of the size compositions of fish they are able to capture, and both should be used together in monitoring and assessing populations of exploited species within partially protected marine areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that

both angler surveys (which can be used to estimate the size composition of the exploited population in an RFH) and fishery-independent sampling (which can be more easily used for estimating abundance of the exploited population) are important components of RFH management and monitoring.
length data collected by angler surveys and by fishery-independent sampling are complementary, with each method having strengths and weaknesses.

the two methods (angler surveys and fishery‐independent surveys) can be used to monitor size composition of fish populations in partially protected marine areas (e.g., recreational fishing havens), but they should be used in a complimentary manner.
